tools.name: record_subject_history
tools.description: One subject's change history and current state from oddly's record, with both clocks on every row: observed_at (when the source says it was true) and fetched_at (when oddly looked), and the receipt hash of each row so any value can be checked with record_verify_receipt. Rate: meter data.history, US$

tools.description: Recompute and check one receipt end to end: the row's receipt hash recomputed from its own sealed document, the link to the row before it, the day root its day folds into, and that root's anchor state (confirmed with a block height, or pending). tools.name: record_answer
tools.description: Answer one question from oddly's record: the newest observed value of one attribute of one subject, with its figure, both clocks, its source, its receipt and its scope. The figure is what the source published when oddly looked, not an estimate, a forecast or advice. Rate: meter data.answer, US$0.001

tools.name: benchmark_categories
tools.description: List the product categories the oddly corpus currently covers, with how many observations and metrics back each one. Call this FIRST to discover valid category paths before calling benchmark_lookup, rather than guessing a path.

tools.name: benchmark_lookup
tools.description: Observed price and assortment benchmarks for a product category: the median and the p25-p75 band across real public storefront listings, with the sample size, the currency, and the exact scope of each figure. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "benchmark_categories" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List the product categories the oddly corpus currently covers, with how many observations and metrics back each one. Call this FIRST to discover valid category …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
